Commentary.Commentary: The first innings of the Super 4 stage clash between India and Sri Lanka in the Asia Cup has concluded, and it was a gripping battle between bat and ball. India, batting first, managed to post a total of 213 runs in their allotted 49.2 overs. The Sri Lankan bowlers were in exceptional form, particularly the spinners, who spun a web around the Indian batsmen on a dry and turning wicket. It was a night where spin reigned supreme, with the Lankan spinners accounting for all the Indian wickets. The Indian innings began with fireworks as skipper Rohit Sharma blazed his way to a quickfire 53 off 48 balls, laced with 7 boundaries and 2 sixes. At one point, India looked comfortable at 80 without loss after 11 overs. However, the tide turned dramatically with the emergence of 20-year-old left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage, who orchestrated a stunning collapse by claiming a five-wicket haul, conceding only 40 runs in his 10 overs. While Ishan Kishan and KL Rahul tried to rebuild the innings, they too fell after crossing the 30-run mark. Charith Asalanka, a part-time off-spinner, chimed in with 4 crucial wickets, dismantling the middle and lower order of the Indian batting lineup. The Sri Lankan spinners exploited the spinning conditions to the fullest, and the Indian batters paid the price for it.

Even though Bangladesh still have an outside chance at this stage, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka look like the real contenders for a place in the final.
